chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not send his wife to the bathhouse.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on sending wives to the bathhouse according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links this recommendation to the broader concept of *iman* (faith), suggesting that modesty (*haya*) is an intrinsic component of belief in the Hereafter. While the ruling is often understood as *mustahabb* (recommended) rather than obligatory, it reflects the Shia emphasis on preserving the sanctity of the marital home and preventing *fitna* (temptation) through the careful management of private spaces. This hadith is frequently cited in discussions on gender segregation and the architectural privacy of traditional bathhouses in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who was a believer in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day, so he should not send his wife to the bathhouse’.
en.sarwar: 29. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Rifa‘ah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who believes in Allah and in the Day of Judgment must not allow his wife to go to a bathhouse.’”
